title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a deliberate attempt to manipulate the training data or citation behavior of large language models by seeding the web with fabricated authoritative sources. A fake think tank published a large volume of text designed to appear like neutral academic research, using specific rhetorical techniques to frame contested facts in a particular direction. The operation ran on a commercial platform explicitly built to optimize content for citation by AI chatbots, meaning the failure point is not inside the models themselves but upstream, in the corpus of text those systems treat as credible when generating responses.

The failure mode is source laundering. AI systems that retrieve or cite web content have no reliable way to distinguish a genuine research institution from a fabricated one that mimics its surface features. No internal model check would catch this, because the content was engineered to pass exactly those checks. Catching it would have required external verification of the institution's existence and funding before any content was ingested or cited, a step that current retrieval and citation pipelines do not routinely perform.

What is not established is whether any major AI system's outputs were actually changed by this content, or to what degree. The reporting describes intent and infrastructure, not measured effect on chatbot responses. The allegation of Israeli government funding and the contracting arrangements described are reported claims, not adjudicated findings.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded operation created a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute to influence artificial intelligence systems into producing pro-Israel propaganda. Between August 6 and 14, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to look like neutral academic research on contentious topics such as genocide allegations and Palestinian casualties. The reports used specific framing techniques, including repeatedly citing a single outdated study about Facebook comments and qualifying casualty figures as coming from "parties to the events," creating an impression that little about Gaza could be established. The operation was built on a commercial platform designed to optimize content for citation by chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude.

The campaign represents part of a much larger Israeli government effort involving tens of millions of dollars routed through European advertising firm Havas Media to shape AI chatbot responses. Records show Israeli government agencies awarded Havas substantial contracts without competitive bidding, and the operation included other ventures such as social media campaigns. Israeli officials have privately expressed frustration that despite heavy spending, the public diplomacy efforts have failed to improve Israel's collapsing American public support, with recent polling showing only 36 percent of Americans sympathize with Israel.
